design.title: Part 1: Design document
design.intro: Write each section below for real, in your own words, addressing Meridian's brief specifically. This isn't a checkbox, submissions are inspected for the specific technical content each section needs, and you'll get told exactly what's missing, not just a pass/fail.

fields.label: Structured output & validation strategy
fields.placeholder: How do you keep model output trustworthy enough for the rest of the system to act on?

fields.label: Context & token budget strategy
fields.placeholder: How do you keep retrieved content plus the conversation within the context window? Name an actual budget.

fields.label: Retrieval & relevance strategy
fields.placeholder: How do you decide what's relevant, and what happens when nothing is? Name an actual threshold and k.

fields.label: Tool execution & idempotency strategy
fields.placeholder: How do you make a retried tool call safe, without duplicating its side effect?

fields.label: Agent control flow strategy

implementation.title: Part 2: Implementation
implementation.intro: Complete the support-request handler below. Real test cases run your actual code, including a genuine repeated-call-ID test.
implementation.frame: Code exercise · Python, runs in a real sandboxed Python interpreter (Pyodide)
implementation.instructions: Complete `async def handle_support_request(input, kb, ticket_tool, seen)`. `input` is `{"queryVector":..., "callId":..., "ticketArgs":...}`. `kb` is a list of `{"id":..., "vector":...}`. Find the KB doc with the highest cosine similarity to `input["queryVector"]`. If its score is below `0.4`, return `{"ok": True, "source": "none", "reason": "no relevant KB match"}` without calling `ticket_tool` at all. Otherwise, check `seen[input["callId"]]` first (return it directly if present), then call `await ticket_tool(input["ticketArgs"])`, caching the result in `seen` only on success, and returning `{"ok": True, "source": "kb", "docId":..., "ticket":...}`. If `ticket_tool` raises, return `{"ok": False, "source": "kb", "docId":..., "error":...}` without caching. Never let this function raise.
implementation.starter:
async def handle_support_request(input, kb, ticket_tool, seen):
    # 1. Find the kb doc with the highest cosine similarity to input["queryVector"].
    #    If the best score is below 0.4, return
    #    {"ok": True, "source": "none", "reason": "no relevant KB match"}
    #    WITHOUT calling ticket_tool at all.

    # 2. Otherwise, check seen[input["callId"]] first. If present, return it directly
    #    (don't call ticket_tool again for a call ID that already succeeded).

    # 3. Otherwise, await ticket_tool(input["ticketArgs"]). On success, cache
    #    {"ok": True, "source": "kb", "docId": ..., "ticket": ...} in seen[input["callId"]] and return it.
    #    On failure, return {"ok": False, "source": "kb", "docId": ..., "error": ...} WITHOUT caching,
    #    so a retry with the same callId gets a real second attempt.

    # YOUR CODE HERE

    pass

tests.name: Below-threshold match returns 'none' without calling the ticket tool
tests.hint: Find the best cosine-similarity score across kb. If it's below 0.4, return {'ok': True, 'source': 'none', 'reason': ...} immediately, never call ticket_tool.

tests.name: A relevant match calls the ticket tool once and returns its result with the correct docId
tests.hint: When the best score is >= 0.4, call ticket_tool(input['ticketArgs']) and return {'ok': True, 'source': 'kb', 'docId': <best match id>, 'ticket': <result>}.

tests.name: The same callId is not re-executed against the ticket tool (idempotency)
tests.hint: Before calling ticket_tool, check if seen[input['callId']] already has a value. If so, return it directly instead of calling the tool again.

tests.name: Different callIds for relevant matches execute independently
tests.hint: Your idempotency check must be keyed by input['callId'] specifically. Two different callIds should both result in a ticket_tool call.

tests.name: A ticket_tool that raises returns a structured failure and is NOT cached, so a retry with the same callId gets a real second attempt
tests.hint: Wrap the ticket_tool call in try/except. On failure, return {'ok': False, ...} WITHOUT writing to seen, so the next call with the same callId calls the tool again.

tests.name: Picks the highest-scoring doc when multiple candidates clear the relevance threshold
tests.hint: Compare EVERY document's score and track the maximum, don't just take the first one that clears 0.4, keep checking the rest for a better match.

debugging.title: Part 3: Debugging
debugging.intro: This code shipped to production and caused an incident. Read it, find the bug, and answer both questions, this tests whether you can recognize a familiar failure mode in code you didn't write.
debugging.q1: Which module's material does this bug violate?
debugging.q2: In one or two sentences, what specifically is wrong, and what would you change?
debugging.answerLabel: What's wrong with the code and what would you change
debugging.placeholder: What's missing, and what's the fix...

options.text: Module 6: the retry has no backoff at all, it retries instantly in a tight loop and never uses jitter, exactly the retry-storm risk
Module 4: the retry function doesn't check an idempotency key before calling the model
options.reason: Retrying this outbound model call isn't a duplicate-tool-execution problem, the idempotency concern from Module 4 is about tool calls with real side effects, a plain model call being retried doesn't have that risk here.

options.text: Module 5: the retry has no step limit at all
options.reason: It does have a bound, attempt >= 5 raises and stops recursing. The problem isn't the absence of a limit, it's that every attempt up to that limit fires instantly with no delay.

review.title: AI Engineering Design Review
review.intro: Ungraded, not checked against an answer key. Before a real engineer calls a system "done," they walk it component by component and ask what happens when that component fails. Do the same here, for the specific Meridian bot you built, not in the abstract.

questions.text: What happens in your implementation when the model returns invalid structure?
questions.placeholder: Trace it through your actual handle_support_request code, not in general...

questions.text: What happens when the relevant information is not retrieved, or nothing clears your relevance threshold?
questions.placeholder: What does the bot say to the user, and does it ever pretend to know something it doesn't...

questions.text: What actions is the model allowed to perform, and what stops it from performing an action it shouldn't?
questions.placeholder: Name the specific validation or permission check, and where in the pipeline it runs...

questions.text: What happens when the same event, the same call ID, arrives twice?
questions.placeholder: Walk through the cache check in your implementation, what's the actual outcome the second time...

questions.text: What prevents this system from looping forever, or from repeating a failing action indefinitely?
questions.placeholder: Name the specific bound, not just \

questions.text: How would you know, with a number, whether a future change to this bot actually improved it?
questions.placeholder: What's in the eval set, what's the baseline, what would count as a regression...
